newsitem.title: SYRIA: Kuwait ministers press anti-Iraq cause.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait ministers press anti-Iraq cause.

text.p: A Kuwaiti envoy visited Egypt and Syria on Tuesday to press the case that the U.S. military buildup in the Gulf was necessary to protect against threats by Iraqi President Saddam Hussein.
Kuwaiti Information Minister Sheikh Saud Nasser al-Saud al-Sabah met Syrian President Hafez al-Assad in Damascus after arriving from Cairo where he had talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.
Official sources said Sheikh Saud was carrying a message concerning Iraqi threats to Kuwait. Sources in Damascus quoted him saying he was explaining "Kuwait's measures to preserve its security."
Kuwait has been the strongest supporter of U.S. action against Iraq, including missile attacks earlier this month and the current military buildup in the Gulf.

"The letter deals with developments in Kuwait and the Gulf after the Iraqi threats...and movements of the Iraqi army which threatens the security and stability of Kuwait," Sheikh Saud said of his message.

Syria and Egypt, both members of the U.S.-led coalition that drove Iraqi occupation forces from Kuwait in 1991, did not support U.S. attacks on Iraq, which followed the entry of Iraqi forces into northern Iraq for the first time in five years.
Sheikh Saud said in Alexandria after talks with Mubarak that he was still taking seriously Baghdad's threats against Kuwait for letting U.S. forces use it as a base for possible attacks on Iraq.
Although Iraq has backed away from its initial warning that Kuwait's action would be an "act of war", Sheikh Saud said: "These statements by the Iraqis are still standing."
Sheikh Saud said: "We don't deal with words but with realities which we see clearly in Iraq's south and these are worrying."
Cairo and Syria, like most of the Arab world, considered Baghdad's military intervention in northern Iraq as the legitimate action of a national government.

In the Gulf, Kuwait's defence minister also sought support from 1991 Gulf War allies. Sheikh Ahmad Hamoud al-Jaber al-Sabah arrived in Saudi Arabia on the first leg of a tour to the other Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states, the official Kuwait News Agency KUNA reported.
